nodes.summary: The decision problem NOT-ALL-EQUAL 3-SAT accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a NOT-ALL-EQUAL 3-SAT instance $(n, \varphi)$ that is well-formed and not-all-equal satisfiable. Every bitstring that decodes to no instance is rejected.
nodes.title: NOT-ALL-EQUAL 3-SAT as a decision problem

nodes.summary: A NOT-ALL-EQUAL 3-SAT instance $(n, \varphi)$, with $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\varphi$ a CNF formula, is not-all-equal satisfiable when there are truth values $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}$ such that, for the assignment $v$ with $v(x) = a_x$ for $x < n$ and $v(x) = \mathrm{false}$ for $x \ge n$, every clause of $\varphi$ contains a literal satisfied by $v$ and a literal not satisfied by $v$.
nodes.title: Not-all-equal satisfiability of an instance

nodes.summary: A NOT-ALL-EQUAL 3-SAT instance is a pair $(n, \varphi)$ of a natural number $n$, the number of variables, and a CNF formula $\varphi$. The formula is not required to have three literals per clause; that is part of well-formedness.
nodes.title: NOT-ALL-EQUAL 3-SAT instances

nodes.summary: The decision problem NOT-ALL-EQUAL 3-SAT over bitstrings belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: NOT-ALL-EQUAL 3-SAT is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A NOT-ALL-EQUAL 3-SAT instance $(n, \varphi)$ is well-formed when every clause of $\varphi$ is a list of exactly three literals, repetitions allowed, and every literal $(x, b)$ in it has variable index $x < n$.
nodes.title: Well-formed NOT-ALL-EQUAL 3-SAT instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
